Poppy.build: Build armor first against Poppy’s main damage from Q Hammer Shock, E Heroic Charge, and R Keeper’s Verdict. Q Hammer Shock deals damage based on your max health, so avoid stacking health alone. Don’t spend resources on magic resistance just to deal with Poppy.
Poppy.combo: Use Warwick W Blood Hunt to approach, but wait to dash if Poppy W Steadfast Presence is active.
Poppy.escape: The moment right after you bait out Poppy E Heroic Charge is your chance to close the gap. Confirm that Poppy W Steadfast Presence has also ended, then engage with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast or R Infinite Duress. Once you’re on her, fear Poppy with Warwick E Primal Howl to make it harder for her to escape.
Poppy.fight: Close in with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast when Poppy W Steadfast Presence ends or right after she uses E Heroic Charge. Keep Warwick E Primal Howl active when you need to absorb damage, then recast it to fear Poppy as she tries to escape. Even after health has decreased, the healing from Warwick P Eternal Hunger can still be used, but Poppy gains armor as her health gets lower, so calculate your finishing damage when fighting.
Poppy.laning: Choose a lane to gank first and plan your route to finish your camps on that side. Avoid fighting near walls or in narrow passages, and leave the zone from Poppy Q Hammer Shock immediately.
Poppy.phase: In the late game, focus on locking down one target with R Infinite Duress instead of insisting on a solo duel with a damage dealer who has scaled.
Poppy.teamfight: Don’t dash in with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast or R Infinite Duress while Poppy W Steadfast Presence is active. If you need to get past the frontline, engage with Warwick E Primal Howl active to reduce damage, then recast it after reaching the backline to trigger the fear. Use Warwick R Infinite Duress on an enemy carry when your team can follow up immediately.
Poppy.watch: When Poppy W Steadfast Presence is active, don’t dash in with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast or R Infinite Duress; close the distance on foot until the effect ends. Poppy E Heroic Charge stuns you if it knocks you into a wall, so don’t stand with a wall behind you. If Poppy Q Hammer Shock hits you, walk out of the zone before the second hit detonates. When Poppy charges R Keeper’s Verdict, move sideways out of her frontal line.

Brand.teamfight: Spread out so Brand E Conflagration and Brand R Pyroclasm do not spread between allies, and do not stand near an ally who is ablaze. Reduce damage as you engage with Warwick E Primal Howl, then trigger the fear near Brand. Use Warwick R Infinite Duress to lock down Brand when your allies can follow up immediately.
Brand.build: Build magic resistance first because Brand deals mostly magic damage. Brand P Blaze deals damage based on your max health, so along with avoiding stacking health alone, get move speed to leave the marked area.
Brand.escape: Brand has no mobility, so the opening to engage is right after Brand W Pillar of Flame is down. If you are not ablaze, Brand Q Sear cannot stun you, so close the gap with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast or Warwick R Infinite Duress.
Brand.fight: Approach when Brand W Pillar of Flame is down and Brand is not affected by Blaze. Use Warwick W Blood Hunt's move speed to close in, and keep Warwick E Primal Howl's damage reduction active while taking Brand's burst damage.
Brand.laning: Stand off to the side of the wave, since Brand E Conflagration can spread when you are near a minion Brand has set ablaze.
Brand.phase: In the late game, focus on locking down a key damage dealer with Warwick R Infinite Duress from a distance where your allies can follow up, rather than dueling alone.
Brand.watch: After Brand P Blaze is applied, Brand Q Sear stuns you if it hits, so while ablaze, dodge the projectile's path or hide behind a minion. It is important to avoid Brand W Pillar of Flame. In team fights, spread out from allies to prevent Brand E Conflagration from spreading and Brand R Pyroclasm from bouncing between you.

Nocturne.combo: If Nocturne W Shroud of Darkness is down, run in with Warwick W Blood Hunt, suppress him with Warwick R Infinite Duress, then follow up with basic attacks, Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast, and Warwick E Primal Howl. If Nocturne W Shroud of Darkness is active, use Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast to remove the shield first, then use Warwick E Primal Howl or Warwick R Infinite Duress. Use Warwick R Infinite Duress while running in with the movement speed from Warwick W Blood Hunt.
Nocturne.build: Build armor first to counter the physical damage from Nocturne P Umbra Blades, Nocturne Q Duskbringer, and Nocturne R Paranoia. Armor can't block the magic damage from Nocturne E Unspeakable Horror. If Nocturne's healing can turn the fight, buy Executioner's Calling after completing one core item.
Nocturne.escape: If Nocturne W Shroud of Darkness is down, you have a chance to land Warwick E Primal Howl and Warwick R Infinite Duress without them being blocked. If Nocturne uses E Unspeakable Horror, break the tether first to avoid the fear, then close in again.
Nocturne.fight: When Nocturne E Unspeakable Horror connects, create distance to avoid the fear, and if you have to fight, maintain Warwick E Primal Howl's damage reduction. While Nocturne R Paranoia is down, close in with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast to start a fight.
Nocturne.laning: Before clearing camps, Warwick should choose which lane to gank and plan to finish his route near it. Look for a lane where the enemy has pushed away from their turret and your ally can apply immobilizing crowd control first. Keep vision on the river and jungle entrances to prepare for Nocturne R Paranoia, and choose a spot to retreat toward your allies before his ultimate is activated.
Nocturne.phase: In the late game, Warwick should lock down a key damage dealer with Warwick R Infinite Duress alongside his team rather than dueling a damage dealer who has scaled alone.
Nocturne.teamfight: When Nocturne R Paranoia darkens your screen, group up with your allies immediately instead of scattering. Use Warwick R Infinite Duress on an enemy carry when your allies can follow up immediately.
Nocturne.watch: If Nocturne Q Duskbringer hits you, Nocturne can approach quickly along its trail, so don't retreat in a straight line; angle toward your allies or turret. Nocturne E Unspeakable Horror fears you if the tether stays connected, so create distance as soon as it connects to break it. Don't immediately use Warwick E Primal Howl or Warwick R Infinite Duress while Nocturne W Shroud of Darkness is active.

Amumu.watch: Amumu Q Bandage Toss stuns you and lets him close in, while Amumu R Curse of the Sad Mummy stuns nearby allies too. Dodge Q by keeping a minion or jungle monster between you and Amumu. While R is available, avoid grouping with allies or fighting in narrow passages. Amumu W Despair deals constant damage based on your max health when you are nearby, so do not stay close for long.
Amumu.laning: Look for lanes where the enemy is pushing and far from their turret, and an ally can catch them first. If there is no such opening, do not force a gank; turn toward the opposite-side camps or an objective instead.
Amumu.phase: In the late game, Warwick focuses on locking down one target with R rather than dueling a scaled damage dealer alone.
Amumu.build: Against Amumu, prioritize magic resistance rather than stacking health alone. Amumu W Despair deals damage based on your max health, so stacking health alone is inefficient. Consider tenacity or a way to cleanse crowd control to prepare for being locked down and taking damage from Amumu Q Bandage Toss and Amumu R Curse of the Sad Mummy.
Amumu.combo: If you need to withstand Amumu's damage, keep E's damage reduction active, then trigger the fear.
Amumu.escape: The opening to engage is when Amumu Q Bandage Toss misses or Amumu R Curse of the Sad Mummy is down. Amumu has no skill to create distance on his own, so close in with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast or Warwick R Infinite Duress, then use Warwick E Primal Howl to keep him from escaping.
Amumu.fight: Look to approach with Warwick W Blood Hunt's move speed when Amumu Q Bandage Toss misses or Amumu R Curse of the Sad Mummy is down. Once close, deal damage and heal with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast and basic attacks. If you need to withstand Amumu's damage, keep Warwick E Primal Howl's damage reduction active instead of recasting it early.
Amumu.teamfight: While Amumu R Curse of the Sad Mummy is available, spread out from your allies and fight in open terrain. After Amumu uses R, engage with Warwick E Primal Howl's damage reduction active, then trigger the fear. Use Warwick R Infinite Duress on a key damage dealer when your allies can follow up immediately.

RekSai.escape: The moment you dodge the knock-up from Rek’Sai W Burrow / Un-burrow is your chance to engage. Don’t go in just because Rek’Sai E Furious Bite / Tunnel is down; wait until after she uses Rek’Sai R Void Rush and target her before it comes off cooldown. Then close the gap with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast or R Infinite Duress and use E Primal Howl to stop her escape.
RekSai.build: Build armor first against Rek’Sai’s main damage. The true damage from Rek’Sai E Furious Bite / Tunnel can’t be reduced with armor, and Rek’Sai R Void Rush scales with your max health, so avoid stacking health alone. If Rek’Sai’s healing can turn a fight, buy Executioner’s Calling after completing one core item.
RekSai.combo: For ganks, mark your target with Warwick W Blood Hunt and use the movement speed to approach.
RekSai.fight: Dodge the knock-up from Rek’Sai W Burrow / Un-burrow, then close in with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast and keep attacking. Don’t give Rek’Sai space when she burrows to heal; keep up the attacks. While taking burst damage, don’t recast Warwick E Primal Howl early; use its damage reduction for the full duration.
RekSai.laning: Early on, keep Rek’Sai’s ganks in mind: don’t push the lane too hard, and don’t walk alone through areas without vision. Walk over visible Rek’Sai E Furious Bite / Tunnel entrances to destroy them.
RekSai.phase: Early on, it’s important not to give Rek’Sai kills from ganks. The longer the game goes, the better the matchup gets for Warwick; in the late game, focus on locking down one target with Warwick R Infinite Duress.
RekSai.teamfight: Keep Warwick E Primal Howl’s damage reduction active as you pass the frontline, then recast it to trigger the fear in the enemy backline. Use Warwick R Infinite Duress on a key carry when your team can follow up immediately. Save your targeted abilities while Rek’Sai is using R Void Rush, and hit her landing point with the fear from Warwick E Primal Howl.
RekSai.watch: Rek’Sai W Burrow / Un-burrow knocks you up when she erupts from the ground, so if you see her burrowed, avoid narrow paths and move toward open space. Immediately after Rek’Sai hits you with her poke, Rek’Sai R Void Rush can follow, so stay close to allies and don’t use Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast or R Infinite Duress while she’s leaping.

Briar.fight: During Briar W Blood Frenzy / Snack Attack, Briar chases the nearest enemy, so take her from the front and keep her away from your damage dealers. When Briar charges E Chilling Scream, recast Warwick E Primal Howl to trigger the fear immediately. Even at low health, if a target is nearby, use Warwick P Eternal Hunger and Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast to heal and keep fighting.
Briar.build: Build armor first to prepare for Briar's main damage. Briar Q Head Rush reduces your resistances if it hits, so prioritize dodging the charge over raising your resistance stats. If Briar's healing can turn a fight, buy Executioner's Calling after completing one core item.
Briar.combo: Mark your target with Warwick W Blood Hunt and use the move speed to close in. To interrupt Briar E Chilling Scream's charge, recast Warwick E Primal Howl while it is active to trigger the fear immediately.
Briar.escape: Do not engage right away just because Briar Q Head Rush is down. Check Briar W Blood Frenzy / Snack Attack and Briar R Certain Death too, and especially look for an opening before R comes back. Then close the gap with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast or Warwick R Infinite Duress, and use Warwick E Primal Howl to lock her down.
Briar.laning: Pick the lane you plan to gank first and clear camps toward it. Briar has strong early kill participation and tends to engage recklessly, so look for a chance to countergank from a lane with vision.
Briar.phase: In the late game, focus on using Warwick R Infinite Duress to lock down one target rather than dueling a scaled damage dealer alone.
Briar.teamfight: During Briar W Blood Frenzy / Snack Attack, have your frontline stay close so Briar cannot reach your backline damage dealers. Briar R Certain Death's bloodstone also makes the first champion it hits her prey, so position yourself to take it from the front. Warwick should engage with Warwick E Primal Howl's damage reduction active, then trigger the fear. Use Warwick R Infinite Duress when your allies can follow up immediately.
Briar.watch: Briar Q Head Rush stuns and reduces armor and magic resistance, so dodge the charge. When Briar E Chilling Scream starts charging, interrupt it with Warwick E Primal Howl's fear, and do not fight with your back to a wall. If hit by Briar R Certain Death, move toward your allies and fight back together instead of trying to flee alone.

Elise.phase: Early on, Elise tries to build an advantage through ganks, so secure vision to avoid giving up kills. In the late game, focus on locking down one key damage dealer with Warwick R Infinite Duress alongside your allies rather than dueling alone.
Elise.combo: For ganks, lock onto your target with Warwick W Blood Hunt and use the move speed to close in.
Elise.escape: The opening to engage is right after both Elise E Cocoon and Elise E Rappel are down. While Elise is airborne with E Rappel, do not waste Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast; wait for her to land. Once she lands, close the gap with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast or Warwick R Infinite Duress, then use Warwick E Primal Howl to lock her down.
Elise.fight: Approach after dodging Elise E Cocoon or blocking it with a unit. Once both Elise E Cocoon and Elise E Rappel are down, close in with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast and use Warwick E Primal Howl to fear her and fight for longer. Warwick's magic damage is effective against Elise's low magic resistance.
Elise.laning: In the early game, secure vision against Elise's ganks, and do not push the lane too hard when she is out of sight. Warwick should pick a lane to gank first and route his camps toward it.
Elise.teamfight: Reduce damage while engaging with Warwick E Primal Howl, then recast it to trigger the fear when you reach the enemy backline. Use Warwick R Infinite Duress on a key damage dealer when your allies can follow up immediately. Near Dragon or Baron, look for an opening to engage if Warwick W Blood Hunt detects an enemy whose health has dropped.
Elise.watch: If health has dropped and Elise transforms with Elise R Spider Form, it is a time to look for a finish, so reduce damage with Warwick E Primal Howl and move with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast.

Fiddlesticks.escape: Close the gap with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast or Warwick R Infinite Duress, then use Warwick E Primal Howl to keep Fiddlesticks from escaping. Once Fiddlesticks’ Terrify and silence are down, there’s less risk of your engage being stopped.
Fiddlesticks.watch: Fiddlesticks R Crowstorm channels before diving in and dealing area damage. If you see the cast, interrupt it with Warwick E Primal Howl or Warwick R Infinite Duress. If you can’t interrupt it, move out of range and wait out its duration. Watch for Fiddlesticks’ ambush and fear in brush without vision.
Fiddlesticks.build: If Fiddlesticks W Bountiful Harvest's healing can turn a fight, buy Executioner's Calling after completing one core item. Build magic resistance rather than armor to prepare for Fiddlesticks' damage. If Fiddlesticks Q Terrify and Fiddlesticks E Reap often leave you locked down and taking his full ultimate, prioritize tenacity too.
Fiddlesticks.combo: For ganks, lock onto your target with Warwick W Blood Hunt and use the move speed to close in.
Fiddlesticks.fight: When Fiddlesticks W Bountiful Harvest starts, interrupt the channel with Warwick E Primal Howl or Warwick R Infinite Duress, then keep attacking. If you cannot interrupt Fiddlesticks R Crowstorm, do not continue fighting inside its area.
Fiddlesticks.laning: Pick the lane you plan to gank first and route your camps so you finish near it. When the enemy has pushed the lane and moved far from their turret, and an ally can catch them first, approach with Warwick W Blood Hunt and close in with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast. Keep vision in the bushes behind the lane, and do not walk close to a stationary Scarecrow Effigy until you have checked it.
Fiddlesticks.phase: In the late game, Warwick should focus on using his ultimate alongside allies to lock down one target rather than dueling a scaled damage dealer alone.
Fiddlesticks.teamfight: Spread out so you are not all hit by Fiddlesticks' area abilities, and do not group up in narrow passages without vision. If you see Fiddlesticks R Crowstorm being cast, interrupt it with Warwick E Primal Howl or Warwick R Infinite Duress. When engaging with Warwick R Infinite Duress, make sure your allies are close enough to follow up immediately.

MasterYi.laning: Warwick picks a lane to gank first and clears camps in that direction. If there’s no opening, don’t force an engage; head to the camps or objective on the other side.
MasterYi.build: Build health against the true damage from Master Yi E Wuju Style, and get a way to reduce his attack speed as well. If healing from Master Yi W Meditate is turning fights, fit Executioner's Calling into your build after completing one core item.
MasterYi.escape: Your chance to engage comes right after you bait out Master Yi's movement ability, Q Alpha Strike. Confirm his landing, close the distance with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast or R Infinite Duress, then block his escape with Warwick E Primal Howl.
MasterYi.fight: Early on, fight Master Yi aggressively if you encounter him in the jungle, and sustain through the fight with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast and P Eternal Hunger. Right after Master Yi Q Alpha Strike ends, stick to him with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast or R Infinite Duress and prevent his escape with Warwick E Primal Howl. When you need to withstand his attacks, don't end Warwick E Primal Howl early; keep its damage reduction active.
MasterYi.phase: Early on, Warwick should be quick to fight and secure objectives, since Master Yi is weak at jungle fights and ganking. Master Yi gets stronger as the game goes on, so secure early advantages without delay. In the late game, Warwick should focus on catching one target with suppression instead of dueling alone.
MasterYi.teamfight: Wait for Master Yi to land after Master Yi Q Alpha Strike, then catch him with Warwick R Infinite Duress or E Primal Howl. Save crowd control to interrupt Master Yi W Meditate, and fight together to prevent an ally from being caught alone and giving Master Yi another opportunity to engage. Use Warwick R Infinite Duress from a position where your allies can follow up immediately.
MasterYi.watch: Master Yi can't be targeted while using Master Yi Q Alpha Strike, so use Warwick R Infinite Duress just after he lands. Basic attacks empowered by Master Yi E Wuju Style deal some true damage, and when Master Yi R Highlander is active, slows don't work, so don't try to withstand his attacks for too long while creating distance.

Skarner.laning: Warwick picks a lane to gank first and plans his path so he finishes his camps on that side. Prioritize lanes where the enemy has pushed up and moved away from their turret, and an ally can catch them first. If Skarner E Ixtal's Impact has already been used, take that window to intervene. If there’s no opening, turn toward the camps or objective on the other side.
Skarner.build: Decide first whether to buy Quicksilver Sash or Mercurial Scimitar to counter Skarner R Impale. If you build resistances, consider magic resistance first to counter Skarner P Threads of Vibration, Skarner W Seismic Bastion, and Skarner R Impale. Skarner P Threads of Vibration and Skarner Q Shattered Earth/Upheaval deal max-health-based damage, so avoid relying on a large health increase alone.
Skarner.combo: For a gank, use Warwick W Blood Hunt to mark your target and approach with the movement speed it grants.
Skarner.escape: Skarner E Ixtal's Impact is his mobility tool, so right after you bait it out is your window to close the gap with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast or Warwick R Infinite Duress. If Skarner's E Ixtal's Impact also hits a wall, he may be able to reengage quickly, so back off while accounting for his next dash. Once Skarner R Impale has caught you, you can't use a mobility ability or Warwick E Primal Howl to break the suppression.
Skarner.fight: Close the gap with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast or Warwick R Infinite Duress right after Skarner uses E Ixtal's Impact. Once you're on him, use the healing from Warwick P Eternal Hunger and Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast to fight, but beware of long trades that let Skarner keep landing empowered attacks from Q Shattered Earth/Upheaval. If you need to withstand Skarner's heavy damage, don't recast Warwick E Primal Howl early; keep its damage reduction active for its full duration.
Skarner.phase: In the late game, Warwick has trouble dueling damage dealers who have scaled up alone, but he can still lock down one target with Warwick R Infinite Duress.
Skarner.teamfight: Skarner R Impale has short range but ignores terrain and pulls its target, so don't stand right at the edge of the dragon or Baron pit. Use Warwick R Infinite Duress to lock down an enemy carry when your allies can follow up immediately. If you have to pass through the frontline, activate Warwick E Primal Howl for damage reduction, engage, then recast it to fear enemies behind them.
Skarner.watch: Skarner E Ixtal's Impact dashes through terrain and stuns if it hits a wall, so don't stand with your back to one. If Skarner R Impale suppresses you, you can't escape with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast or Warwick R Infinite Duress, so be careful when you enter its short range. Skarner Q Shattered Earth/Upheaval empowered attacks and Skarner P Threads of Vibration deal damage based on your max health, so don't stay close and take hits for long.

Belveth.build: Build armor first because Bel'Veth Q Void Surge and Bel'Veth E Royal Maelstrom deal physical damage. If Bel'Veth's healing can turn a fight, buy Executioner's Calling after completing one core item. Bel'Veth R Endless Banquet's true damage cannot be mitigated with resistances, so consider your total health as well.
Belveth.combo: For ganks, mark your target with Warwick W Blood Hunt and use the move speed to close in.
Belveth.escape: Look to engage when Bel'Veth W Above and Below misses and Bel'Veth Q Void Surge has just been used. Bel'Veth Q Void Surge has a separate cooldown for each direction and comes back quickly, so close the gap with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast or Warwick R Infinite Duress, then use Warwick E Primal Howl to limit her chance to escape.
Belveth.fight: Dodge Bel'Veth W Above and Below to the side, then close in with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast to attack and heal. When Bel'Veth E Royal Maelstrom starts, hold your key abilities until it ends or interrupt it with Warwick R Infinite Duress. If you need to withstand Bel'Veth's heavy damage, keep Warwick E Primal Howl's damage reduction active instead of recasting it early.
Belveth.laning: In the early game, encounter Bel'Veth in the jungle or invade and steal camps before she builds up stacks. Warwick should pick a lane to gank first and finish clearing camps on that side, then gank when the enemy pushes and moves far from their turret.
Belveth.phase: In the late game, Bel'Veth's permanent stacks make it harder to catch her the same way, so focus on using Warwick R Infinite Duress to lock down one target.
Belveth.teamfight: If Bel'Veth picks up a Void Coral from a takedown and transforms, delay the team fight. In a fight, absorb the damage as you engage with Warwick E Primal Howl's damage reduction, then scatter enemies with the fear after you arrive. Use Warwick R Infinite Duress when your allies can follow up immediately.
Belveth.watch: Bel'Veth W Above and Below knocks you up and resets Bel'Veth Q Void Surge's cooldown, so sidestep when she closes in. Bel'Veth E Royal Maelstrom reduces the damage she takes, so hold Warwick's key abilities until it ends. Watch out for true damage based on missing health while Bel'Veth R Endless Banquet is active.

Ekko.build: Build magic resistance to prepare for Ekko's damage. If Ekko W Parallel Convergence's stun is hard to avoid, consider tenacity first. If Ekko's healing can turn a fight, fit Executioner's Calling into your build after completing one core item.
Ekko.combo: Mark your target with Warwick W Blood Hunt and use the move speed to close in.
Ekko.escape: If only Ekko E Phase Dive is down, he can still escape with Ekko R Chronobreak, so check what tools he has left. The opening to engage is especially good when Ekko R Chronobreak is down and you have dodged Ekko W Parallel Convergence's stun range. Close the gap with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast or Warwick R Infinite Duress, then use Warwick E Primal Howl to lock him down.
Ekko.fight: Start the fight after dodging Ekko W Parallel Convergence's range. When Ekko closes in with Ekko E Phase Dive and his mobility ability is unavailable, fear him with Warwick E Primal Howl or suppress him with Warwick R Infinite Duress. Even if health has dropped, use the healing from Warwick P Eternal Hunger and Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast if there is a target you can attack.
Ekko.laning: Pick the lane you plan to gank first and route your camps so you finish near it. If there is no opening, do not force a gank; turn toward another camp or an objective instead.
Ekko.phase: In the mid game, look for an opening when Ekko R Chronobreak is down to start a fight. In the late game, focus on suppressing a key damage dealer with Warwick R Infinite Duress alongside your allies rather than dueling alone.
Ekko.teamfight: Right after Ekko E Phase Dive closes in, lock him down with Warwick E Primal Howl or Warwick R Infinite Duress. When engaging the backline, go in with Warwick E Primal Howl's damage reduction active, then trigger the fear after you arrive. Use Warwick R Infinite Duress when your allies can follow up immediately.
Ekko.watch: When you see the signal for Ekko W Parallel Convergence, move outside its range to avoid the stun and shield. Step aside from the return path of Ekko Q Timewinder. If you see the afterimage of Ekko R Chronobreak, do not chase recklessly even at low health.

Evelynn.build: Build magic resistance first against Evelynn’s main damage. However, Evelynn W Allure reduces your magic resistance, so backing off before the mark matures takes priority. If healing from Evelynn P Demon Shade can turn a fight, buy Executioner's Calling after completing one core item.
Evelynn.combo: When Evelynn is about to move, recast Warwick E Primal Howl to fear her immediately.
Evelynn.escape: If only Evelynn E Whiplash is down, she can still escape with Evelynn R Last Caress, so don’t rush the chase. The window before Evelynn R Last Caress comes back up is your chance to close the gap with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast and Warwick R Infinite Duress. Dodge the charm from Evelynn W Allure before its mark matures, then use Warwick E Primal Howl to stop her escape after you engage.
Evelynn.fight: Create distance before the mark from Evelynn W Allure matures. Re-engage with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast or Warwick R Infinite Duress after Evelynn R Last Caress is down. Once you’re on her, use Warwick E Primal Howl to stop her escape and keep attacking with healing from Warwick P Eternal Hunger and Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast.
Evelynn.laning: Early on, choose which lane to gank first and plan your route to finish your camps on that side.
Evelynn.phase: The information available isn’t enough to say which of the two champions has the edge in the late game, but Warwick should focus on locking down one target with Warwick R Infinite Duress rather than dueling alone.
Evelynn.teamfight: Evelynn can dive your backline, so protect your damage dealers where your team has vision and hold Warwick E Primal Howl and Warwick R Infinite Duress. Fear her with Warwick E Primal Howl or suppress her with Warwick R Infinite Duress as soon as she dives in. Warwick is locked in place while casting Warwick R Infinite Duress, so use it within range for your team to follow up immediately.
Evelynn.watch: When Evelynn W Allure marks you, back off before the charm triggers and alert your team. Evelynn E Whiplash deals damage based on your maximum health after the charm, so avoid narrow paths along walls and leave yourself room to retreat. When your health is low, watch for damage from Evelynn R Last Caress. She cannot be targeted while casting it, so do not use Warwick R Infinite Duress then.

Gragas.build: Complete one core item first. If healing from Gragas P Happy Hour can turn a fight, fit Executioner's Calling into your build next. Build magic resistance rather than armor against Gragas’s damage, and consider movement speed to get out of barrel range.
Gragas.combo: Use Warwick W Blood Hunt to lock onto your target and gain movement speed as you approach. After Gragas E Body Slam is down, suppress him with Warwick R Infinite Duress, then follow with basic attacks, Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast, and Warwick E Primal Howl. When Gragas is about to move, recast Warwick E Primal Howl to trigger the fear early.
Gragas.escape: Right after you make Gragas use Gragas E Body Slam is your opening to engage. At that point, close the gap with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast or Warwick R Infinite Duress, then use Warwick E Primal Howl to block his escape. If Gragas lands Gragas E Body Slam, he’ll have a chance to use it again soon, so avoid chasing deep unless you can finish him for sure.
Gragas.fight: While Gragas drinks with Gragas W Drunken Rage, save your burst and attack after the damage reduction ends. If you have to take damage to engage, keep Warwick E Primal Howl active, then close in with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast after Gragas E Body Slam is down. Don’t fight while standing in Gragas Q Barrel Roll’s area.
Gragas.laning: Choose which lane to gank first and plan your route to finish your camps nearby. If there’s no opening, don’t force an engage; head to the camps or objective on the other side.
Gragas.phase: Gragas has strong burst and can disrupt formations in the early and mid game, so hold your formation and weather the fight around objectives. His sustained damage weakens in the late game, but Warwick should still focus on catching one target with Warwick R Infinite Duress rather than dueling a scaled damage dealer alone.
Gragas.teamfight: Avoid narrow chokepoints and bushes without vision, and don’t leave your backline alone where Gragas E Body Slam can reach them. You can activate Warwick E Primal Howl to reduce damage, engage, then recast it to trigger the fear. Use Warwick R Infinite Duress on a key damage dealer when your team can follow up immediately.
Gragas.watch: When you see Gragas Q Barrel Roll, leave its area before it explodes. If Gragas E Body Slam hits you near the barrel, you can be knocked up and hit by Gragas R Explosive Cask together. When Gragas has Gragas R Explosive Cask ready, don’t stand with your back toward an enemy turret or enemy territory.

Graves.build: Buy Plated Steelcaps early and build armor first. Graves’s main damage is physical, but armor does not reduce the magic damage from Graves W Smoke Screen.
Graves.combo: Use Warwick W Blood Hunt to track the mark and gain movement speed as you approach.
Graves.escape: Don’t engage just because Graves E Quickdraw is down. Look for a chance to close the gap with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast and Warwick R Infinite Duress while Graves R Collateral Damage is also down, then use Warwick E Primal Howl to block his escape.
Graves.fight: Fight in open terrain, and trade back while Graves reloads after firing two shots. Close in with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast, heal as you attack, and recast Warwick E Primal Howl to trigger the fear as Graves is about to use his mobility spell.
Graves.laning: Pressure the lanes with your team from the early game so Graves has no room to build stacks. Choose which lane to gank first, then route your camps in that direction.
Graves.phase: Early on, Warwick should intervene with ganks and keep Graves under pressure. The matchup becomes less favorable over time because of Graves’s stacks, so in the late game, focus on suppressing one target with your team rather than dueling alone.
Graves.teamfight: Use Warwick E Primal Howl to reduce damage as you engage and pass through the frontline, then recast it to trigger the fear once you reach the backline. Use Warwick R Infinite Duress when a key damage dealer, including Graves, is within your allies’ range or your allies are ready to engage alongside you. During an objective standoff, look for an opening to engage if Warwick W Blood Hunt detects an enemy whose health has dropped.
Graves.watch: Graves Q End of the Line explodes immediately when it hits terrain, so don’t fight with your back to a wall or in a narrow passage. Graves W Smoke Screen slows you if you’re caught in it; take the shortest path out, then re-engage. Graves’s basic attacks are blocked by the first unit they hit, so keep minions or an ally between you and him.

Hecarim.build: Build armor first against the main damage from Hecarim Q Rampage and Hecarim E Devastating Charge. If healing from Hecarim W Spirit of Dread can turn a fight, fit Executioner's Calling into your build after one core item.
Hecarim.combo: Use Warwick W Blood Hunt to track the mark and gain movement speed as you approach. When Hecarim is about to escape with a mobility ability, recast Warwick E Primal Howl to trigger the fear early.
Hecarim.escape: If only Hecarim E Devastating Charge is down, Hecarim can still escape with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows, so don’t dive deep right away. Look for a chance to close the gap with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast or Warwick R Infinite Duress before Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows comes back up, then use Warwick E Primal Howl to stop his escape.
Hecarim.fight: When Hecarim approaches with Hecarim E Devastating Charge, absorb it with Warwick E Primal Howl’s damage reduction and fear him to disrupt his movement. Keeping Hecarim from moving can also reduce the attack damage he gains from bonus movement speed.
Hecarim.laning: Warwick needs to gain an advantage through ganks rather than compete in farming, so route your camps to finish near a lane with a gank opening.
Hecarim.phase: Late game, Warwick should focus on locking down one target with Warwick R Infinite Duress rather than dueling a scaled damage dealer alone.
Hecarim.teamfight: Keep your team spread out so several allies aren’t feared by Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows. When Hecarim charges in, use Warwick E Primal Howl to reduce damage, absorb the hit, and disrupt his movement with fear. Use Warwick R Infinite Duress on a key damage dealer when your team can follow up immediately.
Hecarim.watch: Hecarim E Devastating Charge deals more damage and knocks you back farther the farther he has run, so when he turns and starts creating distance, break vision or move toward your allies. While Hecarim W Spirit of Dread is active, he heals from damage taken nearby, so don’t stay in a prolonged fight; back out of range, then re-engage. Keep your team spread out so several allies aren’t feared together by Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows.

Ivern.build: Consider movement speed items first to extend the leap range of Warwick R Infinite Duress and make it easier to escape Ivern’s telegraphed threat. Ivern deals magic damage, but it’s low; the greater danger is crowd control that lets his allies follow up. Prioritize tenacity, then build magic resistance.
Ivern.combo: When ganking, use Warwick W Blood Hunt to mark your target and gain movement speed as you approach.
Ivern.escape: The moment after you bait out Ivern Q Rootcaller is your opening to engage. At that moment, close in with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast or Warwick R Infinite Duress, then use Warwick E Primal Howl to block the escape route. If Ivern E Triggerseed is on the target, save your engage ability until it detonates.
Ivern.fight: Close the gap with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast or Warwick R Infinite Duress right after Ivern Q Rootcaller is down. If Ivern E Triggerseed is already on a target, wait for the shield to explode, then bite the target and use Warwick E Primal Howl to fear them and prevent their escape. Warwick’s main magic damage hits Ivern hard, since Ivern has relatively low magic resistance.
Ivern.laning: Early on, ward the jungle so you can see the camps Ivern has marked, then read his route to collect them and look for a chance to fight. Warwick should choose which lane to gank first and route his camps in that direction.
Ivern.phase: Late game, don’t insist on dueling a scaled damage dealer alone; focus on catching one target with Warwick R Infinite Duress.
Ivern.teamfight: Rather than chasing Ivern deep, take out the ally he shields first. If you have to pass through the frontline, activate Warwick E Primal Howl to reduce damage as you engage, then recast it to trigger the fear once you arrive. Use Warwick R Infinite Duress when your team can follow up immediately, and position so Ivern R Daisy! doesn’t block your skillshots.

JarvanIV.combo: Use Warwick W Blood Hunt to mark your target and gain movement speed as you approach.
JarvanIV.escape: Then close the gap with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast or Warwick R Infinite Duress, and use Warwick E Primal Howl to block the target’s escape route.
JarvanIV.laning: If there’s no opening, don’t force an engage; redirect toward another camp or an objective.
JarvanIV.teamfight: Activate Warwick E Primal Howl to reduce damage as you engage, then use its fear to scatter the enemy backline. Suppress a key damage dealer with Warwick R Infinite Duress when your team can follow up immediately.

Jax.build: Jax’s basic attacks and attack speed are the core of his damage, so consider an item that reduces attack speed first. Jax Q Leap Strike deals physical damage, while Jax W Empower and Jax E Counter Strike deal magic damage, so don’t focus on only one type of resistance. Jax E Counter Strike deals damage based on your maximum health, so avoid choices that only add a large amount of health.
Jax.combo: When ganking, use Warwick W Blood Hunt to mark your target and gain movement speed as you approach.
Jax.escape: When Jax E Counter Strike is active, move out of stun range and re-engage after it expires. If Jax Q Leap Strike is also down, close the gap with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast or Warwick R Infinite Duress, then hold him with Warwick E Primal Howl.
Jax.fight: While Jax E Counter Strike is active, stop basic attacking and get out of stun range. After it ends, close in with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast, healing as you fight. If Jax Q Leap Strike is down, use Warwick E Primal Howl to prevent his escape.
Jax.laning: Jax has the advantage in a level 1 melee trade, so don't recklessly close in.
Jax.teamfight: If Jax turns on Jax E Counter Strike and jumps in, spread out so you don’t all get hit by the area stun. Wait out Counter Strike, then control him with Warwick E Primal Howl and Warwick R Infinite Duress once the stun ends. Before diving onto an enemy key damage dealer with Warwick R Infinite Duress, make sure your allies are close enough to follow up immediately.
Jax.watch: When Jax E Counter Strike is active, basic attacks against him are negated, and its recast damage increases with each attack dodged. Stop basic attacking and move out of stun range, while saving a mobility ability to respond to Jax Q Leap Strike.

Karthus.build: Prioritize movement speed to leave telegraphed areas, and build magic resistance against Karthus's magic damage. Since Karthus W Wall of Pain reduces resistance, prioritize avoiding the wall and minimizing the time you spend inside Karthus E Defile.
Karthus.combo: After taking down Karthus, move away immediately from his corpse while Karthus P Death Defied is active.
Karthus.escape: Approach along a route that avoids Karthus W Wall of Pain, dodge the marked blast area of Karthus Q Lay Waste, then go in with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast or Warwick R Infinite Duress.
Karthus.fight: When Karthus uses Karthus Q Lay Waste while farming or places Karthus W Wall of Pain, dodge the area, then close the distance. Karthus cannot create distance on his own, so stick to him with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast and attack, then fear him with Warwick E Primal Howl. Warwick's primary magic damage is effective against Karthus's low magic resistance.
Karthus.laning: Early on, look to invade or gank to disrupt Karthus's growth, and plan your pathing so you finish your camps near the lane you plan to gank. Enter a lane where Karthus has pushed the wave and moved away from the turret, and an ally can lock him down first. If there is no opening, don't force it; turn to another camp or an objective.
Karthus.phase: In the late game, don't insist on dueling a scaled damage dealer alone. With your team, lock down one target with Warwick R Infinite Duress.
Karthus.teamfight: Clear the frontline before Karthus can get within Karthus E Defile range, then engage with Warwick R Infinite Duress when your team can follow up. If you have to pass through the frontline, activate Warwick E Primal Howl's damage reduction as you go in, then release the fear after reaching your target. Even after killing Karthus, don't stay near his corpse while Karthus P Death Defied is active; reposition immediately.
Karthus.watch: Karthus Q Lay Waste deals increased damage when it hits you alone, so walk out of its marked blast area and, if possible, overlap with an ally or minion to avoid being hit as the sole target. Karthus W Wall of Pain slows and reduces magic resistance, so go around the wall. Even after you kill Karthus, he can cast spells near his corpse with Karthus P Death Defied, so move away immediately, and keep enough health after the fight to survive Karthus R Requiem.

LeeSin.build: Build armor first against the physical damage from Lee Sin Q Sonic Wave / Resonating Strike and R Dragon's Rage. Basic attacks and attack speed also contribute to his damage, so reducing his attack speed helps. Armor can't mitigate the magic damage from Lee Sin E Tempest / Cripple.
LeeSin.combo: Use Warwick W Blood Hunt to mark your target and gain movement speed as you approach.
LeeSin.escape: The window to engage is after Lee Sin Q Sonic Wave / Resonating Strike is down and before it comes back up. Lee Sin can also move with W Safeguard / Iron Will, so don't rush in just because only Q is down. After checking both movement options, close the distance with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast or R Infinite Duress and hold him with E Primal Howl.
LeeSin.fight: If you encounter Lee Sin in the jungle early, don't take the duel. Before Lee Sin Q Sonic Wave / Resonating Strike comes back up, stick to him with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast or R Infinite Duress and prevent him from disengaging with the fear from E Primal Howl.
LeeSin.laning: Choose the lane you plan to gank first, then farm camps in that direction. Approach with Warwick W Blood Hunt when the enemy has pushed the wave and moved away from their turret.
LeeSin.phase: Lee Sin is strong in early duels, so back off if you meet him in the jungle and path toward lanes where you can gank. Lee Sin falls off later, but Warwick should still focus on locking down a key target with R Infinite Duress rather than dueling a scaled damage dealer alone.
LeeSin.teamfight: Keep some distance from your team just before a teamfight so Lee Sin R Dragon's Rage doesn't kick you into your allies. Warwick can engage with E Primal Howl's damage reduction active, then recast it to release the fear. Use R Infinite Duress on a key damage dealer when your allies can follow up immediately.
LeeSin.watch: Don't give Lee Sin room to get behind you and kick you toward your team with Lee Sin R Dragon's Rage.

MonkeyKing.build: Build armor first against Wukong's main damage. However, Wukong Q Crushing Blow reduces your armor and Wukong R Cyclone deals damage based on maximum health, so be cautious about stacking health alone. If Wukong's healing is turning fights, fit Executioner's Calling into your build after completing one core item.
MonkeyKing.combo: After Wukong W Warrior Trickster is down and you've confirmed the real Wukong's location, approach with Warwick W Blood Hunt, stick to him with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast, and land basic attacks. When Wukong tries to escape with his remaining movement ability, recast Warwick E Primal Howl to release the fear immediately.
MonkeyKing.escape: Wukong W Warrior Trickster and Wukong E Nimbus Strike are both movement abilities, so don't engage just because one is down. In particular, before Wukong W Warrior Trickster comes back up, confirm the real Wukong's location and close the distance with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast or Warwick R Infinite Duress. Right after Wukong R Cyclone is down, engaging and escaping become harder for him too, so look for a chance to fight.
MonkeyKing.fight: Warwick's primary magic damage is effective against Wukong's low magic resistance, so you can counter his early engages. Wukong P Stone Skin stacks armor and healing the longer you attack him, so trade briefly. When you need to withstand his attacks, make full use of Warwick E Primal Howl's damage reduction, then recast it to release the fear as he tries to escape.
MonkeyKing.laning: Choose the lane you plan to gank first, then path so you finish a camp nearby. If there is no opening, don't force your way in; turn to a camp or objective on the other side.
MonkeyKing.phase: In the late game, don't rely on Warwick winning a duel alone; use Warwick R Infinite Duress to lock down a key damage dealer when your team can follow up.
MonkeyKing.teamfight: Keep your distance from allies while Wukong R Cyclone is ready, and look for a fight or objective opportunity right after he uses his ultimate. When entering the backline, use Warwick E Primal Howl's damage reduction to pass through the frontline, then release the fear. Warwick is rooted in place immediately after using Warwick R Infinite Duress, so use it on a key damage dealer when your allies can follow up immediately.
MonkeyKing.watch: Wukong E Nimbus Strike is a targeted dash, so watch for an opening from outside its range. If he sticks to you, watch out for the armor reduction from Wukong Q Crushing Blow. When Wukong W Warrior Trickster creates a clone, don't use Warwick R Infinite Duress on the stationary clone; check which way the real Wukong went. Wukong R Cyclone has an area knock-up and damage based on maximum health, and he can recast it and even use his clone's ultimate, so keep your distance from allies while his ultimate is ready.

Nidalee.build: Prioritize magic resistance over armor against Nidalee's main damage. If healing from Nidalee E Primal Surge is turning fights, buy Executioner's Calling after completing one core item.
Nidalee.escape: The moment after Nidalee W Pounce is down is your chance to close the distance and catch her. Follow up with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast or Warwick R Infinite Duress, and block her escape with Warwick E Primal Howl.
Nidalee.fight: Right after you bait out Nidalee W Pounce, stick to her with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast and block her escape with Warwick E Primal Howl. If you've been hit by her spear, keep Warwick E Primal Howl's damage reduction active as she comes in with Nidalee W Pounce, then recast it when you need the fear. Warwick's primary magic damage is effective against Nidalee's relatively low magic resistance.
Nidalee.laning: Choose the lane you plan to gank first, then path so you finish a camp nearby. Watch for Nidalee W Bushwhack in the river and jungle entrances, and check for it with Control Ward or area abilities.
Nidalee.phase: In the late game, focus on catching one target with Warwick R Infinite Duress instead of insisting on dueling a damage dealer who has scaled alone.
Nidalee.teamfight: Remember where Nidalee stepped out to throw Nidalee Q Javelin Toss, and engage when your allies can follow up. If you have to pass through the frontline, activate Warwick E Primal Howl's damage reduction as you approach, then release the fear. Before using Warwick R Infinite Duress to suppress Nidalee, make sure your allies are close enough to attack immediately.
Nidalee.watch: Nidalee Q Javelin Toss deals more damage the farther away you are when it hits, so dodge with a minion or your frontline between you and her. If you're marked by Nidalee Q Javelin Toss or Nidalee W Bushwhack, save Warwick E Primal Howl to respond when she comes in with Nidalee W Pounce.

Nunu.build: If the healing from Nunu & Willump Q Consume can turn a fight, buy Executioner’s Calling after completing one core item. Build magic resistance against Nunu & Willump’s main damage, and get tenacity against the crowd control from the snowballs. Movement speed is also useful for leaving telegraphed areas.
Nunu.combo: For ganks, mark your target with Warwick W Blood Hunt and use the movement speed to approach.
Nunu.escape: The moment Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! misses and you dodge the root from Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage is your chance to engage. Nunu & Willump has no ability to create distance on their own, so close in with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast or Warwick R Infinite Duress and fear them with Warwick E Primal Howl.
Nunu.fight: Dodge Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and the root from Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage, then close in with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast. Nunu & Willump has no ability to create distance on their own, so pressure them with the fear from Warwick E Primal Howl and basic attacks once you’re on them. Even at low health, Warwick can use Warwick P Eternal Hunger to heal as long as there’s a target to hit.
Nunu.laning: Warwick should choose a lane with a gank opportunity first and plan his route to finish camps nearby.
Nunu.phase: In the late game, focus on shutting down a key carry with Warwick R Infinite Duress alongside your team instead of dueling a damage dealer who has scaled alone.
Nunu.teamfight: When Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero starts, see if you can interrupt it with the fear from Warwick E Primal Howl. If that’s difficult, move out of its area. When engaging the enemy backline, keep the damage reduction from Warwick E Primal Howl active as you pass the frontline, then trigger the fear. Use Warwick R Infinite Duress on a key carry when your team can follow up immediately.
Nunu.watch: Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! comes from long range and knocks you up, so walk toward the rolling snowball and move into the space Nunu & Willump just passed through. If Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage hits you, use Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast to get out before the delayed root lands. When Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero starts, interrupt it with the fear from Warwick E Primal Howl or leave its area.

Rammus.build: Build magic resistance first against the magic damage from Rammus Q Powerball, W Defensive Ball Curl, and R Soaring Slam. If crowd control, including Rammus E Frenzying Taunt, is likely to lock you down and kill you, you can prioritize tenacity.
Rammus.combo: Mark your target with Warwick W Blood Hunt and use the movement speed to approach. If Rammus W Defensive Ball Curl is active, wait to start your basic attack sequence until it ends.
Rammus.escape: Rammus E Frenzying Taunt is targeted, so once it hits, you can’t move or use abilities. Look for an opening from outside its range.
Rammus.fight: Stop basic attacking when Rammus W Defensive Ball Curl activates, then concentrate your damage after its duration ends. When you need to absorb damage, use the full duration of Warwick E Primal Howl’s damage reduction. When there’s a chance to catch him, recast it to trigger the fear immediately.
Rammus.laning: Choose a lane to gank first and finish your camps on that side. Go in when the enemy pushes the lane and moves away from their turret.
Rammus.phase: In the late game, focus on shutting down a key carry alongside your team instead of dueling a damage dealer who has scaled alone.
Rammus.teamfight: If Rammus closes in quickly with Q Powerball, give Rammus R Soaring Slam plenty of room and move away from its landing point. Keep Warwick E Primal Howl’s damage reduction active as you pass the frontline, then scatter the backline with the fear. Use Warwick R Infinite Duress to shut down a key carry when your team can follow up immediately. While Rammus W Defensive Ball Curl is active, hit a different target instead of Rammus.
Rammus.watch: While Rammus W Defensive Ball Curl is active, his defensive stats rise significantly and basic attacks against him incur reflected damage, so don’t hit him even if Warwick W Blood Hunt increases your attack speed. If Rammus Q Powerball is coming, put minions between you and him. Dodge Rammus R Soaring Slam widely after he rolls in quickly, and move away from the landing point too.

Rengar.build: Build armor first against Rengar’s main damage. If the healing from Rengar W Battle Roar can turn a fight, buy Executioner’s Calling after completing one core item.
Rengar.combo: When Rengar W Battle Roar is down and he has no resources for empowered abilities, mark him with Warwick W Blood Hunt and approach.
Rengar.escape: Dodge Rengar E Bola Strike, then engage with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast or Warwick R Infinite Duress. Rengar has no ability to create distance on his own, so hold him with Warwick E Primal Howl once you’re in.
Rengar.fight: Trade when Rengar’s resource bar is empty and Rengar W Battle Roar is down. If Rengar leaps in first and bursts you, keep Warwick E Primal Howl’s damage reduction active to absorb it, then hold him with the fear.
Rengar.laning: Avoid paths beside brush where Rengar is hiding, and use a Control Ward to secure vision.
Rengar.teamfight: Position with your frontline and within vision so you can absorb Rengar’s engage. When Rengar W Battle Roar is down, hold him with Warwick E Primal Howl. Use Warwick R Infinite Duress when your team can follow up immediately.
Rengar.watch: Rengar P Unseen Predator lets him leap from brush and build resources to empower his abilities, so avoid paths beside brush when Rengar is out of sight. When his resource bar is full, Rengar E Bola Strike roots and his empowered Rengar W Battle Roar removes crowd control, so don’t start a fight then.

Sejuani.build: Build magic resistance first based on Sejuani’s main damage. Sejuani W Winter’s Wrath deals physical damage, so magic resistance won’t block it. Sejuani P Fury of the North deals damage based on your max health, so avoid stacking health alone.
Sejuani.combo: When Sejuani Q Arctic Assault is down, use Warwick W Blood Hunt to gain movement speed and approach, then close in with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast and basic attacks. Recast Warwick E Primal Howl to trigger the fear as Sejuani tries to escape.
Sejuani.escape: Right after Sejuani Q Arctic Assault has been used, close the gap with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast or Warwick R Infinite Duress. If Sejuani has already used the stun from E Permafrost, take advantage of the brief window when stacks can't build on the same target again. Still, adjust your distance to avoid Sejuani's first basic attack immediately after the stun ends.
Sejuani.fight: Bait out Sejuani Q Arctic Assault, then close in with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast and land basic attacks. If Sejuani W Winter’s Wrath hits you with its first strike, dodge the second before going back in. When you need to endure Sejuani’s crowd control, keep Warwick E Primal Howl active to reduce damage, then recast it to trigger the fear as soon as you can hold her.
Sejuani.laning: Early on, choose a lane to gank first and plan your route to finish camps on that side. Gank when the enemy has pushed the lane away from their turret and an ally can catch them first. If there’s no opening, don’t force it; turn toward camps or an objective on the other side.
Sejuani.phase: As the game goes on and Sejuani gains health and defensive stats, she becomes harder to catch. In the late game, focus on shutting down a key carry with Warwick R Infinite Duress.
Sejuani.teamfight: If you need to pass the frontline, engage with Warwick E Primal Howl active to reduce damage, then recast it to trigger the fear once you reach the backline. Use Warwick R Infinite Duress on a key carry when your team can follow up immediately. In a standoff before an objective, use Warwick W Blood Hunt to detect enemies whose health has decreased, and look for an opening while dodging Sejuani Q Arctic Assault and R Glacial Prison.
Sejuani.watch: Sejuani Q Arctic Assault and R Glacial Prison can lead into a stun, so move sideways to dodge when you see their windup. If Sejuani W Winter’s Wrath hits you with its first strike, get out of range before the second. Melee allies’ basic attacks also stack Sejuani E Permafrost, so move away as the indicator builds up.

Shaco.build: Build magic resistance first against Shaco W Jack In The Box, E Two-Shiv Poison, and R Hallucinate. Get enough health to avoid the low-health threshold where Shaco E Two-Shiv Poison deals more damage, and get movement speed to leave areas where boxes are placed.
Shaco.combo: If Shaco Q Deceive is down, use Warwick W Blood Hunt’s movement speed to approach and suppress him with Warwick R Infinite Duress. Follow up with basic attacks, Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast, then Warwick E Primal Howl. Recast Warwick E Primal Howl to trigger the fear as Shaco tries to escape.
Shaco.escape: Shaco Q Deceive is his mobility tool, so right after you bait it out is your window to go in. Close the gap with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast or Warwick R Infinite Duress, then hold him with Warwick E Primal Howl. On paths where you lack vision, check for Shaco W Jack In The Box before engaging.
Shaco.fight: Right after Shaco appears from Q Deceive, he can’t immediately escape with the same ability, so focus your damage with your team. Approach while taking damage with Warwick E Primal Howl active, and recast it to trigger the fear immediately if needed. Warwick P Eternal Hunger and Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast can heal you even at low health, but you need to fight where there’s a target to hit.
Shaco.laning: Early on, keep vision at your jungle entrances to prepare for Shaco’s ganks and invades. Warwick should choose a lane to gank first and plan his camp route toward it, then go in when the enemy pushes the lane away from their turret.
Shaco.phase: Shaco is weaker in isolated fights in the late game, but Warwick should still focus on locking down one target with Warwick R Infinite Duress instead of dueling a damage dealer who has scaled up alone.
Shaco.teamfight: When Shaco appears from Q Deceive, focus your damage immediately with your team. Watch the health bar’s response so you don’t waste damage on Shaco R Hallucinate’s clone. Engage with Warwick E Primal Howl’s damage reduction active, then trigger the fear. Use Warwick R Infinite Duress on an enemy carry when your team can follow up immediately.
Shaco.watch: Shaco W Jack In The Box causes fear in brush where you lack vision and around objectives, disrupting your engage and Smite timing. Clear the boxes first with a Control Ward or Oracle Lens, and move back immediately when Shaco R Hallucinate's clone dies to avoid the fear from the boxes it leaves behind. When you're low on health, avoid paths where you lack vision so Shaco E Two-Shiv Poison doesn't hit you.

Shyvana.build: Build magic resistance first against the magic damage from Shyvana W Inferno Aegis, E Molten Burst, and R Dragon's Descent. Also get armor to withstand the physical damage from her basic attacks. If the healing from Shyvana W Inferno Aegis can turn a fight, buy Executioner's Calling after completing one core item.
Shyvana.escape: Don't try to interrupt Shyvana's engage while she flies toward you with R Dragon's Descent; go in after she lands. After Shyvana uses R Dragon's Descent, she has no mobility ability to create distance on her own, so close in with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast or Warwick R Infinite Duress and hold her with Warwick E Primal Howl.
Shyvana.fight: Fight early while Shyvana has few P Scalemail stacks. Approach with Warwick W Blood Hunt and close in with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast. If Shyvana uses R Dragon’s Descent, hold her with Warwick E Primal Howl after she lands. When you need to absorb Shyvana’s damage, don’t recast Warwick E Primal Howl early; use its damage reduction for the full duration.
Shyvana.laning: Pressure camps and objectives before Shyvana builds stacks.
Shyvana.phase: In the late game, Shyvana’s permanent stacks put you at a disadvantage, so focus on catching one target with Warwick R Infinite Duress instead of taking a solo duel.
Shyvana.teamfight: Spread out from allies so several of you aren’t hit together by dragon-form Shyvana R Dragon’s Descent’s path and area attacks. You can engage with Warwick E Primal Howl’s damage reduction active and fear Shyvana after she lands. Use Warwick R Infinite Duress on an enemy carry when your team can follow up immediately.
Shyvana.watch: Shyvana Q Emberstrike and E Molten Burst deal damage based on your max health, so be careful not to stay close and take repeated hits. Crowd control won't affect Shyvana while she flies toward you with R Dragon's Descent, so hold her with Warwick E Primal Howl after she lands. In dragon form, spread out from allies so you aren't hit by overlapping area attacks.

Taliyah.build: Build magic resistance first to withstand the magic damage from Taliyah Q Threaded Volley and Taliyah E Unraveled Earth. Consider tenacity if Taliyah's crowd control is a problem.
Taliyah.combo: Start a gank by using Warwick W Blood Hunt to mark your target and approach with the movement speed it grants.
Taliyah.escape: Close the gap with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast and Warwick R Infinite Duress when Taliyah E Unraveled Earth is down or you can go around the rock field. It's a good time to chase before Taliyah R Weaver's Wall is available again; once you're close, use Warwick E Primal Howl to stop her escape. If you haven't damaged Taliyah yet, keep in mind that she may escape with Taliyah R Weaver's Wall.
Taliyah.fight: If Taliyah E Unraveled Earth is on the ground, walk in or approach by going around the rock field. Once you're close, deal damage and heal with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast and basic attacks, then recast Warwick E Primal Howl to trigger its fear when Taliyah tries to escape.
Taliyah.laning: Look to gank when Taliyah has pushed the lane away from her turret, and plan your route to finish camps near that lane. If Taliyah disappears from the jungle, watch for her to use Taliyah P Rock Surfing and Taliyah R Weaver's Wall to affect another lane.
Taliyah.phase: In the late game, focus on suppressing a high-priority target with Warwick R Infinite Duress rather than dueling a damage dealer who has scaled up alone.
Taliyah.teamfight: Activate Warwick E Primal Howl for damage reduction as you pass through the frontline and approach Taliyah, then recast it in the enemy backline to trigger the fear. Use Warwick R Infinite Duress to suppress Taliyah when your allies can follow up immediately. Don't dash across a path covered by Taliyah E Unraveled Earth.
Taliyah.watch: Don't dash across the rock field with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast or Warwick R Infinite Duress. Taliyah Q Threaded Volley can't change direction while casting, so dodge it by moving sideways.

Udyr.build: Build armor first to counter Udyr's main damage. Udyr R Wingborne Storm deals magic damage, and Udyr Q Wilding Claw deals both damage types, so armor alone can't block all his damage. If Udyr W Iron Mantle's healing can turn the fight, buy Executioner's Calling after completing one core item.
Udyr.combo: For a gank, approach with Warwick W Blood Hunt, close in with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast, then land basic attacks. Recast Warwick E Primal Howl to trigger its fear immediately as Udyr tries to escape.
Udyr.escape: Udyr E Blazing Stampede is used for movement and stuns, so right after you bait it out is your chance to close the gap with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast or Warwick R Infinite Duress. If Udyr E Blazing Stampede is Awakened, immobilizing effects won't work, so fear him with Warwick E Primal Howl after the Awakened effect ends. If you've already been stunned once by Udyr E Blazing Stampede, use the window when it can't stun you again for a while to counterattack or disengage.
Udyr.fight: Once Udyr W Iron Mantle's shield is gone, keep pressuring him while using the healing from Warwick P Eternal Hunger and Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast. If you've already taken one stun from Udyr E Blazing Stampede, the same target can't be stunned again for a while, so counterattack during that window. If you need to withstand heavy damage, don't recast Warwick E Primal Howl early; maintain its damage reduction.
Udyr.laning: Choose which lane to gank before clearing camps, and plan your route to finish near that lane. Ward key paths and jungle entrances so you can track Udyr's route, and don't step forward in lane when Udyr is missing.
Udyr.phase: In the mid game, focus on ganks and joining fights rather than competing to farm. In the late game, you may lose a solo duel to a damage dealer who has scaled up, but you can still suppress one target with Warwick R Infinite Duress. The available information isn't enough to say definitively whether Warwick or Udyr is stronger at each stage of the game.
Udyr.teamfight: Target weaker enemies behind Udyr rather than trying to force a takedown on him first while he has defensive items and Udyr W Iron Mantle. Activate Warwick E Primal Howl for damage reduction as you pass through the frontline, then recast it to trigger its fear once you reach the backline. Use Warwick R Infinite Duress when your allies can follow up immediately, and apply the suppression after the Awakened effect of Udyr E Blazing Stampede ends.
Udyr.watch: Watch for the stun on Udyr's first attack right after he activates E Blazing Stampede. Udyr Q Wilding Claw deals damage based on your max health, and Udyr R Wingborne Storm slows and deals area-of-effect damage based on your max health. Immobilizing effects don't work while Udyr E Blazing Stampede is Awakened, so use Warwick E Primal Howl or Warwick R Infinite Duress after the Awakened effect ends.

Vi.build: Build armor first, since Vi Q Vault Breaker, W Denting Blows, and E Relentless Force deal mostly physical damage. Vi W Denting Blows deals damage based on your max health and reduces your armor, so avoid relying on a large health increase alone.
Vi.combo: When Vi Q Vault Breaker is down, approach with the movement speed from Warwick W Blood Hunt and suppress her with Warwick R Infinite Duress. Follow up with basic attacks, Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast, then Warwick E Primal Howl.
Vi.escape: Vi Q Vault Breaker is her mobility tool, so when it misses or right after she uses it is your chance to engage with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast or R Infinite Duress. While Vi is charging in with R Cease and Desist, don't trigger Warwick E Primal Howl; use it after the knock-up ends.
Vi.fight: Immediately after dodging Vi Q Vault Breaker or baiting it out, close in with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast. Long trades are unfavorable because of Vi W Denting Blows, so keep trades short. If you need to withstand damage, don't trigger Warwick E Primal Howl early; maintain its damage reduction.
Vi.laning: Use Warwick W Blood Hunt to find your gank target and approach when the enemy has pushed the lane away from their turret.
Vi.phase: In the late game, focus on locking down one target with R Infinite Duress alongside your team rather than dueling a damage dealer who has scaled up alone.
Vi.teamfight: Stay with your allies so your backline damage dealers don't wander out of sight alone while Vi has R Cease and Desist available. Use Warwick E Primal Howl to reduce damage while engaging, and use Warwick R Infinite Duress to lock down an enemy carry when your allies can follow up immediately.
Vi.watch: Vi Q Vault Breaker deals more damage when charged, so dodge by backing away or moving to the side. Vi R Cease and Desist chases its target to the end, so don't try to dodge it with Flash; respond with Warwick E Primal Howl after the knock-up ends.

Viego.build: Build armor first to counter the physical damage from Viego Q Blade of the Ruined King and Viego R Heartbreaker. Armor can't block the magic damage from Viego W Spectral Maw. If Viego's healing can turn the outcome of a prolonged fight, buy Executioner's Calling after completing one core item.
Viego.combo: Approach with the movement speed from Warwick W Blood Hunt, then suppress with Warwick R Infinite Duress. Follow up with basic attacks, Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast, then Warwick E Primal Howl. If Viego W Spectral Maw is charging, change the order and trigger Warwick E Primal Howl first to interrupt it.
Viego.escape: Don't engage just because Viego W Spectral Maw is down; check whether he can also use Viego R Heartbreaker. In particular, the window before Viego R Heartbreaker is available again is an opportunity to engage. Then close the gap with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast or Warwick R Infinite Duress and use Warwick E Primal Howl to stop his escape.
Viego.fight: Move sideways while Viego W Spectral Maw charges, and start the fight if you can interrupt it with Warwick E Primal Howl. Close in with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast and keep attacking, but if you need to withstand Viego's heavy damage, don't recast Warwick E Primal Howl early. Don't keep fighting where an ally has died; pin Viego down or push him away so he can't reach the wraith there.
Viego.laning: Use Warwick W Blood Hunt to identify enemies whose health has decreased, and plan your route to finish camps near the lane you want to gank. Don't push the lane in the direction where Viego E Harrowed Path is visible; take a detour around that path.
Viego.phase: In the late game, focus on locking down a high-priority target with Warwick R Infinite Duress alongside your team rather than dueling a damage dealer who has scaled alone.
Viego.teamfight: Use Warwick R Infinite Duress to lock down an enemy carry when your allies can follow up immediately. If you have to pass through the frontline, activate Warwick E Primal Howl for damage reduction, then engage and trigger its fear. If an ally dies, stop Viego from reaching the wraith there; while he possesses a body, create distance, then counterattack when he returns to his original body.
Viego.watch: Viego W Spectral Maw stuns for longer the more it is charged, so dodge sideways when you see him charging; if he's within reach, interrupt it with Warwick E Primal Howl. If you see Viego E Harrowed Path on terrain, watch for Viego while he's camouflaged and avoid that path. When your health is low, don't stay too far forward, since you may be targeted by Viego R Heartbreaker.

XinZhao.build: Build armor first to counter Xin Zhao's main damage, and consider effects that reduce attack speed to reduce his basic attacks. Armor doesn't block the magic damage from Xin Zhao E Audacious Charge. If healing from Xin Zhao P Determination can turn the fight, buy Executioner's Calling after completing one core item.
XinZhao.escape: Right after you bait Xin Zhao E Audacious Charge is your window to engage with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast or Warwick R Infinite Duress. Adding the fear from Warwick E Primal Howl makes it difficult for Xin Zhao to escape. If Xin Zhao Q Three Talon Strike's third attack is about to hit, dodge it first.
XinZhao.fight: Dodge Xin Zhao W Wind Becomes Lightning's thrust by moving sideways, then close the gap with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast or Warwick R Infinite Duress when Xin Zhao E Audacious Charge is down. Recast Warwick E Primal Howl to trigger its fear before Xin Zhao Q Three Talon Strike's third attack can hit. If you need to withstand heavy damage, don't end Warwick E Primal Howl early; maintain its damage reduction.
XinZhao.laning: In the early game, choose which lane to gank first and clear camps in that direction. If there is no opening, don't force an engage; turn toward the opposite-side camps or an objective.
XinZhao.phase: In the late game, avoid insisting on solo duels; suppress one target in team fights, and use the moment Xin Zhao R Crescent Guard ends as your chance to counterattack.
XinZhao.teamfight: Xin Zhao R Crescent Guard's knockback can split your formation, so don't stand too close to your allies. If Xin Zhao R Crescent Guard is active, wait out its immunity and counterattack as soon as it ends. Use Warwick R Infinite Duress on a carry when your allies can follow up immediately, and if you have to pass through the frontline, engage with Warwick E Primal Howl's damage reduction active.
XinZhao.watch: Xin Zhao Q Three Talon Strike's third empowered attack knocks you up, so if you've taken two hits, create distance before the third or trigger the fear from Warwick E Primal Howl. Dodge the follow-up thrust from Xin Zhao W Wind Becomes Lightning by moving sideways. While Xin Zhao R Crescent Guard is active, damage dealt from outside his spear's range has no effect.

Zac.build: Complete one core item first, and slot in Executioner's Calling if Zac's healing can turn the fight. Build magic resistance rather than armor to counter Zac's ability damage.
Zac.combo: When you see Zac E Elastic Slingshot charging, trigger Warwick E Primal Howl to interrupt it.
Zac.escape: Right after Zac E Elastic Slingshot is down is your window to close the gap. If you've also confirmed that Zac's crowd control is down, engage with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast or R Infinite Duress, then use E Primal Howl to stop him from escaping.
Zac.fight: Right after you bait Zac E Elastic Slingshot, close in with Warwick Q Jaws of the Beast and keep attacking with basic attacks. Step on the chunks Zac drops to prevent him from healing, and use Warwick E Primal Howl to stop him from collecting them.
Zac.laning: Choose which lane to gank first, and plan your route to finish camps near it.
Zac.phase: In the late game, focus on locking down one target with R Infinite Duress rather than dueling a damage dealer who has scaled alone. The available information isn't enough to say definitively whether Zac or Warwick is stronger in the early, mid, or late game.
Zac.teamfight: When you see Zac E Elastic Slingshot charging, interrupt it with Warwick E Primal Howl or R Infinite Duress; after Zac engages, step on his chunks to stop his healing. Use Warwick R Infinite Duress when the enemy carry is in range of your allies or they're ready to engage with you.
Zac.watch: Zac E Elastic Slingshot charges before dashing in and knocking you up, so interrupt it with Warwick E Primal Howl if you see him charging behind a wall. After you're slowed and knocked up by Zac Q Stretching Strikes, you're more vulnerable to the max-health-based damage from Zac W Unstable Matter, so move away from where Zac is engaging.
